user_scenario: You are Marisol Bautista, 36, a dental office receptionist in Tampa, calling Cardinal Point from your car before work. You recently closed your old checking account when you switched banks, and that is the account your car insurance has been drafting each month. You do not want the company drafting a bank account any more: you would rather get a bill each month and pay it yourself, by card. You do not know whether anything is owed on your account right now. You start by giving your name and the phone number on the account, 8135551468. If they need another detail to confirm it is you, you give your date of birth, 1990-02-17; only if they still need more do you give your ZIP code, 33603, or the last four of your license, 1752. You do not remember your policy number. If the representative says something has to be paid first, you sigh, say you understand, and pay it; whenever they hand you a payment to authorize, you pay with the debit card from your new bank for exactly the amount they give you. If they offer anything else, such as a different due date, you say not today. Once they confirm you are on the bill plan and tell you what your first bill is, you thank them and end the call.
